nodes.text: the heart buried in sin
and forgetful of its own light.
They say that the roaming demons,
happy in the darkness of the nights,
terrified when the cock crows,
scatter in fear and give way.
For the hated nearness
of light, of salvation, of the divine,
when the stagnant gloom of darkness is broken,
puts the henchmen of night to flight.
That this is the sign, those who foreknow it
know well: [the sign] of the promised hope,
your forehead and the place of your heart
let the figure of the cross sign them.
The cross drives away all sin;
darkness flees from the cross:
dedicated by such a sign,
the mind does not know how to waver.
Away, O away, you portents
of wandering dreams;
away with you and your stubborn
doings, you deceiver.
